title: Apprenticeship credential exchange
background: A fictional federation links credential records to people while preserving separate employers and training episodes. Person identifiers are local to issuing bodies; two people may share an employer address or contact agent.
observations: A pooled scorer was developed on long-standing issuers. A newly joining issuer changed its person-ID allocation policy, but the transition date is not supplied. Its feed includes corrections and revocations that can arrive after newer messages.

An acceptance rule for equal bare person IDs runs before a contradictory verified credential-holder date rule. Monthly reference labels are produced by that acceptance policy and reviewed only when an employer disputes them.
Entity membership is persisted, while published credential status is cached separately. Engineers propose swapping in the new scorer and reusing both stores because input record IDs have not changed.

A dashboard combines accepted-link agreement and successful-task throughput. Staff can instead keep issuers separate and use only confirmed issuer-qualified identities while investigating ambiguous records.
constraints: False person associations can disclose qualifications to the wrong employer. Revoked credentials must not silently reappear.
No production edits or private-data access are authorized. The decision committee needs reversible options and separately stated evidence and operational gates.
request: Prepare the committee decision: compare the available approaches, define a controlled onboarding/change study, and state when to proceed, hold, or gather more information.
